_measured: 2026-09-04 (Flash dialect slice; the .kitty side is the packaged table's, unchanged)
_scope: The Flash build's authored map bytes ONLY. One unsigned byte per cell, row-major, 188 x 84 (FLASH_PS:41, :17); the game embeds exactly one map (FLASH_MAP) rather than shipping level FILES, so this table has no census and no level-file list. The .kitty end is the same one game as the RWIA table's and its blocks are byte-identical to it -- see censuses._note.
_licence: Derived FACTS with citations. Ships no Hamumu/Raptis bytes: no art, no level data, no source text beyond quoted identifiers and line references.

sources.FLASH_MAP: SWF DefineBinaryData xplor.PlayState_mapData -- the Flash RWK level, 188*84 = 15792 B
sources.RWIA_BIN: 'Robot Wants It All' Steam install ./rwia (ELF-64, NOT stripped). Read-only disassembly of RWKLevel::* / RWKRobot::* / RWKState::UnitFactory.
sources.RWKLF: ~/CC/rwklevelfiles/rwk/tilesets/*.json (GPLv3; used ONLY for the ten style NAMES -- the name->bucket mapping below is re-derived from their stored paint values)

gif._id_space: one authored unsigned byte per cell of the Flash build's embedded map (FLASH_MAP), row-major -- the loader reads it with readUnsignedByte (FLASH_PS:170-176) and indexes it as i % mapWidth / i / mapWidth (FLASH_PS:194, :204, :271). Width and height are constants beside the loader (FLASH_PS:41 mapWidth=188, :17 mapHeight=84), NOT fields of the file: a reader has to be told them.
gif.solid_rule: Flash: solid iff id >= 50 (FlxTilemap.collideIndex, set at FLASH_PS:179; the comparisons are FLASH_TM:202, :348, :400). There is no upper bound, so the rule alone makes 254/255 solid -- but the loader clears both cells to 0 when it spawns the robot and the kitty (FLASH_PS:192-206), so no cell ever holds one at collision time.
gif.drawn_rule: Flash: id >= 1 is drawn (drawIndex = 1, FLASH_PS:180; the comparison is FLASH_TM:309). Id 0 is the only id the tilemap skips.

16.name: ACID, submerged frame 16 (LETHAL on contact)
16.refuse: the Flash lethal range. Player.update probes the tile at (x+7, y+7) and calls Die() on any id in 16..23 (FLASH_PL:377-380). The loader WRITES 16 and 20 itself, from an authored acid source (id 6): 20 where the cell above is air, 16 otherwise (FLASH_PS:219-231). So an id in this range in a map FILE is either a generated value fed back in or a level from the other dialect -- where 16 is SUPERSTAR, 17..21 are the combo letters, 22 the time orb and 23 the secret passage, four kinds of bonus. Converting one of those as Flash would turn a bonus into a death trap, so it is refused by name rather than mapped.

kitty_file.spawn_from_pixel: world = (col*tile_size_px, row*tile_size_px) -- NO half-tile offset. Measured in the program that READS the gif: RWIA_BIN LoadLevel @0x261dc8 (robot, id 255) and @0x261b20 (kitty, id 254) both do imul col,[tileW] / imul row,[tileH] and store the products straight into the entity Point.  The C++ side then normalises: World::LoadLevel (CPP_WC:481) calls Robot::FixPosition, which lifts the collide box out of solid and drops it to the floor (CPP_PC:322-341), so Y moves at load while X does not.  (Note World::GridToWorld, CPP_WC:200, is CENTRE-based -- cell*40+20 -- which is why campaign spawns look half-tile shifted.)

settings_donor.why: it is the flagship acceptance pair's own level, and it carries the SHORTER form of BOTH optional parts: the 71-byte extra chunk (no trailing mDied byte) and the cells-only grid chunk (no mLevelMap array).  The two go together -- see kitty_file.grid_chunk: the 5 levels with mLevelMap are exactly the 5 with the 72-byte extra chunk.  The VALUES are not load-bearing either way: all 11 campaign levels carry byte-identical values for every field of this chunk.

editor_tool_chunk.note: mPaintID is the editor's next paint-REGION id. A writer that paints n regions must leave this above the highest paintID it wrote.

settings_donor.runtime_only_fields: customDraw and extraData are 0 in ALL 11 campaign levels -- they are computed at load (CPP_WC:2790-2806), so a writer must emit 0.

censuses._note: The gif-side census is EMPTY on purpose, and empty is a fact here rather than a gap. The RWIA table's censuses.gif_id_counts is keyed by level FILE name, because that game loads a level out of a set of shipped .gif files and a custom level is an overwrite of one of them. The Flash build has no such set: it embeds exactly ONE map inside the SWF (FLASH_MAP), so there are no file names to key on and no per-file counts to publish. Which ids that one map authors was measured elsewhere and stays there -- it is content, and this repository ships none. Consequently IdTable.gif_level_files is [] for this dialect, and 'authorable' here is derived from the SOURCE (an id the loader or the runtime writes carries an 'observed' note with its line) rather than cross-checked against a count. The .kitty-side censuses are the packaged table's, unchanged, because the .kitty side is the same one game.
